proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M\). All conditional moments used below exist by \(\texttt{ass:moment-radius}\), and conditioning on cohort \(c\) is legitimate because \(p_c\geq p_\star>0\) by \(\texttt{ass:positive-shares}\). Write \(\mathcal L=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma)\). By \(\texttt{ass:rank-two-factor-law}\) and \(\texttt{ass:error-mean}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\nu_c
&=\mathbb E_P[J_cY_i(0)\mid C_i=c]\\
&=\mathbb E_P[\Gamma_{S_c}\lambda_i+\varepsilon_{i,S_c}\mid C_i=c]\\
&=\Gamma_{S_c}m_c.                                             \tag{1}
\end{aligned}
\]
By \(\texttt{ass:loading-error-orthogonality}\) and \(\texttt{ass:conditional-homoskedasticity}\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
V_c
&=\operatorname{Cov}_P(\Gamma_{S_c}\lambda_i+\varepsilon_{i,S_c}\mid C_i=c)\\
&=\Gamma_{S_c}H_c\Gamma_{S_c}^{\prime}
  +\operatorname{Cov}_P(\varepsilon_{i,S_c}\mid C_i=c)\\
&=\Gamma_{S_c}H_c\Gamma_{S_c}^{\prime}+\sigma_c^2I_{|S_c|}.    \tag{2}
\end{aligned}
\]
The first summand in (2) has rank two and second eigenvalue at least \(g_\star>0\) by \(\texttt{ass:local-signal-gap}\). Hence the two leading eigenvalues of \(V_c\) strictly exceed \(\sigma_c^2\), while all remaining eigenvalues equal \(\sigma_c^2\). It follows that
\[
\Pi_2(V_c)=\Pi_{\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})},
\qquad
Q_c=I_{|S_c|}-\Pi_{\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})}.           \tag{3}
\]
The complete observed law \(P_O\) determines \(p_c\), the conditional mean \(\nu_c\), and the conditional covariance \(V_c\), because \(p_c>0\). Therefore it determines every local plane in (3).

Choose the matrices \(B_c\) as in \(\texttt{def:relation-operator}\). Since \(B_c^{\prime}B_c=Q_c\), for every \(y\in\mathbb R^{|S_c|}\),
\[
\|B_cy\|^2=y^{\prime}Q_cy,
\]
so \(\ker B_c=\ker Q_c=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})\). The positive weights \(p_c\) then give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal K(P):=\ker\overline R(P)
&=\bigcap_{c=1}^C\ker(B_cJ_c)\\
&=\left\{x\in\mathbb R^T:x_{S_c}\in
       \operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})\text{ for every }c\in[C]\right\}. \tag{4}
\end{aligned}
\]
In particular, \(\mathcal L\subseteq\mathcal K(P)\). Although the individual orthonormal row bases \(B_c\) are not unique, (4) shows that \(\mathcal K(P)\) is uniquely determined by \(P_O\).

By \(\texttt{lem:generic-rank-two-coordinate-projection-certificate}\), on the generic locus imposed by \(\texttt{ass:generic-factor-rows}\), the local planes in (3) determine \(\mathcal L\) uniquely if and only if the anchor multihypergraph contains a set \(F\) of \(T-2\) triples satisfying
\[
|F'|\leq |V(F')|-2
\qquad\text{for every nonempty }F'\subseteq F.                  \tag{5}
\]
By \(\texttt{def:pebble-certificate}\), (5) is equivalent to \(r_{1,2}(H_3)=T-2\). Such an \(F\) necessarily spans \([T]\), because (5) with \(F'=F\) yields
\[
T-2=|F|\leq |V(F)|-2\leq T-2.                                 \tag{6}
\]

We now relate uniqueness to the linear kernel in (4). If \(\mathcal K(P)=\mathcal L\), any two-dimensional subspace whose restrictions equal the planes in (3) is contained in \(\mathcal K(P)=\mathcal L\), and hence equals \(\mathcal L\). Conversely, suppose the local planes uniquely determine \(\mathcal L\) but \(\mathcal K(P)\supsetneq\mathcal L\). Choose \(h\in\mathcal K(P)\setminus\mathcal L\) and a basis \(u_1,u_2\) of \(\mathcal L\). For \(z\neq0\), set
\[
\mathcal L_z=\operatorname{span}(u_1+zh,u_2).                   \tag{7}
\]
Because \(h\notin\mathcal L\), \(\mathcal L_z\neq\mathcal L\). Equation (4) gives \((\mathcal L_z)_{S_c}\subseteq\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})\). At \(z=0\), each restriction has rank two by \(\texttt{ass:local-signal-gap}\). For each cohort choose a nonzero two-by-two minor of the restricted basis at \(z=0\). Each chosen minor is continuous in \(z\); since \(C<\infty\), all remain nonzero for every sufficiently small \(|z|>0\). Thus \((\mathcal L_z)_{S_c}\) has dimension two and
\[
(\mathcal L_z)_{S_c}=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})
\qquad\text{for every }c\in[C],                                \tag{8}
\]
contradicting uniqueness. Consequently,
\[
r_{1,2}(H_3)=T-2
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathcal K(P)=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma).                       \tag{9}
\]
In particular, if the certificate fails, (9) gives the strict inclusion asserted in the theorem, and the construction (7)--(8) gives the distinct compatible two-dimensional factor plane.

Suppose now that \(r_{1,2}(H_3)=T-2\). Let \(U\) be any orthonormal basis of the observed-law kernel \(\mathcal K(P)\). By (9) and \(\Gamma^{\prime}\Gamma=I_2\) from \(\texttt{ass:factor-normalization}\), there is an orthogonal matrix \(W\in\mathbb R^{2\times2}\) such that \(U=\Gamma W\). The local signal gap implies that \(\Gamma_{S_c}\), and therefore \(U_{S_c}\), has full column rank, so \(U_{S_c}^{\prime}U_{S_c}\) is positive definite and invertible. With \(G_c=\Gamma_{S_c}^{\prime}\Gamma_{S_c}\), equation (1) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
U(U_{S_c}^{\prime}U_{S_c})^{-1}U_{S_c}^{\prime}\nu_c
&=\Gamma W(W^{\prime}G_cW)^{-1}W^{\prime}G_cm_c\\
&=\Gamma WW^{\prime}G_c^{-1}WW^{\prime}G_cm_c\\
&=\Gamma m_c\\
&=\mu_c(P).                                                \tag{10}
\end{aligned}
\]
Here the last equality is the causal response-surface identity following from the factor outcome equation and the conditional mean-zero error restriction; it is not a definition of the causal target. Replacing \(U\) by \(UW_0\) for any orthogonal \(W_0\) leaves the left side of (10) unchanged. Every object on that side is determined by \(P_O\), so (10) is exactly the observed-law map in \(\texttt{def:counterfactual-functional}\). If \(P_0,P_1\in\mathcal M\) have \((P_0)_O=(P_1)_O\), their values in (10) coincide for every cohort and time coordinate. This proves entire-observed-law identification when the certificate passes.

It remains to show why the algebraic conclusion under certificate failure cannot be strengthened to causal-target nonidentification under the frozen assumptions. Consider the allowed specification \(T=4\), \(C=1\), and \(S_1=\{1,2,3\}\). Its anchor hypergraph has one edge, hence
\[
r_{1,2}(H_3)=1<T-2=2.                                      \tag{11}
\]
Let
\[
G_0=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\\1&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix},
\qquad
\Gamma_0=G_0(G_0^{\prime}G_0)^{-1/2}.                       \tag{12}
\]
Since \(G_0^{\prime}G_0\) is positive definite, \(\Gamma_0^{\prime}\Gamma_0=I_2\). The three two-by-two minors formed from the rows indexed by \(S_1\) are \(1\), \(1\), and \(-1\) before right normalization and remain nonzero afterward. Thus the local restriction has rank two and is generic for this one-edge relation matroid.

Fix \(v>0\), take \(p_1=1\), set \(v_\star=v^\star=v\), and let \(\lambda_i\) be uniform on the circle of radius \(\sqrt{2v}\) in \(\mathbb R^2\). Then
\[
\mathbb E[\lambda_i]=0,
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}(\lambda_i)=vI_2,
\qquad
\mathbb E\|\lambda_i\|^{4+\delta}=(2v)^{(4+\delta)/2}.       \tag{13}
\]
Set \(\varepsilon_i=0\) almost surely, choose
\[
M_{\mathrm{mom}}=(2v)^{(4+\delta)/2},
\qquad
0<g_\star<\lambda_2(\Gamma_{0,S_1}vI_2\Gamma_{0,S_1}^{\prime}), \tag{14}
\]
and choose any \(p_\star\in(0,1)\). Equations (12)--(14) verify rank, normalization, positive loading covariance, local signal gap, conditional homoskedasticity with \(\sigma_1=0\), loading-error orthogonality, and the common moment bound. Independent sampling then gives a nonempty model satisfying every frozen primitive restriction.

For precisely the tight radii in (14), the already-established \(\texttt{lem:tight-moment-radius-forces-zero-means}\) gives
\[
\mu(P)=0\qquad\text{for every }P\in\mathcal M.                \tag{15}
\]
Thus, in this nonempty certificate-failing specification, the causal target is the constant observed-law functional zero even though (9) implies generic factor-plane nonuniqueness. Equations (11)--(15) prove that certificate failure alone does not imply the existence of two observed-law-equivalent laws with different missing means, completing the narrowed theorem.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: Apply the published rank-two deterministic count certificate to the canonical anchor hypergraph. For every \(P\in\mathcal M\) with generic factor rows, if \(r_{1,2}(H_3)=T-2\), then every coordinate of \(\mu(P)\) is a functional of the entire observed law \(P_O\), and that functional is the construction in \(\texttt{def:counterfactual-functional}\). If \(r_{1,2}(H_3)<T-2\), then \(\ker\overline R(P)\supsetneq\operatorname{col}(\Gamma)\), and there is a two-dimensional subspace \(\widetilde{\mathcal L}\neq\operatorname{col}(\Gamma)\) such that \((\widetilde{\mathcal L})_{S_c}=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})\) for every \(c\in[C]\). Thus certificate failure implies generic nonuniqueness of the factor plane. It does not, under the frozen primitive assumptions alone, imply causal-target nonidentification: those assumptions permit a nonempty certificate-failing specification on which \(\mu(P)=0\) for every \(P\in\mathcal M\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen tight-moment-radius specialization can force \(\mu(P)=0\) throughout a nonempty certificate-failing model. Therefore certificate failure implies generic factor-plane nonuniqueness, but the current if-and-only-if causal identification claim and its complete-observed-law countermodels do not follow from the frozen assumptions.

proposed.statement: Apply the published rank-two deterministic count certificate to the canonical anchor hypergraph. For every \(P\in\mathcal M\) with generic factor rows, if \(r_{1,2}(H_3)=T-2\), then every coordinate of \(\mu(P)\) is a functional of the entire observed law \(P_O\), and that functional is the construction in \(\texttt{def:counterfactual-functional}\). If \(r_{1,2}(H_3)<T-2\), then \(\ker\overline R(P)\supsetneq\operatorname{col}(\Gamma)\), and there is a two-dimensional subspace \(\widetilde{\mathcal L}\neq\operatorname{col}(\Gamma)\) such that \((\widetilde{\mathcal L})_{S_c}=\operatorname{col}(\Gamma_{S_c})\) for every \(c\in[C]\). Thus certificate failure implies generic nonuniqueness of the factor plane. It does not, under the frozen primitive assumptions alone, imply causal-target nonidentification: those assumptions permit a nonempty certificate-failing specification on which \(\mu(P)=0\) for every \(P\in\mathcal M\).
proposed.justification: The contribution transports the published generic count certificate into an explicit complete-observed-law identifying functional when the certificate passes, and identifies generic factor-plane nonuniqueness as the strongest unconditional conclusion when it fails.
proposed.gap: The published rank-two count criterion does not itself derive the cohort conditional moments, recover the local eigenspaces from the full observed law, or prove that their relation kernel yields the causal untreated means. The frozen class is too broad for a converse in causal-target values.
proposed.consumer: A passing certificate licenses complete untreated-mean recovery for the \(\operatorname{apm}\) and \(\operatorname{fect}\) workflows; a failing certificate diagnoses factor-plane ambiguity but is not by itself a causal impossibility certificate.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(\widehat\mu_c=\operatorname{clip}_{[-B,B]^T}\!\left\{\widehat U(\widehat U_{S_c}^{\prime}\widehat U_{S_c})^{-1}\widehat U_{S_c}^{\prime}\widehat\nu_c\right\},\qquad \mathcal R_N\lesssim\min\{1,(Ns_N^2)^{-1}\},\quad \mathcal W_{N,\alpha}\lesssim\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\), with \(\widehat\theta\) and \(\widehat\rho_N\) defined by robust joint-moment blocks. These are unconditional upper guarantees on nonempty shells. A frontier-scale testing pair on a nondegenerate frozen-model subclass and a model-specific honest-width lower bound remain open; \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\) is sufficient, not necessary in the tight-radius zero-target class.
proposed_core_edits.reason: Remove the discarded model-specific lower-frontier and necessity promises while retaining the unconditional point-estimation and honest-width upper guarantees.

prose_updates.tldr: Short panels with systematic missing outcomes require gluing cohort-specific covariance eigenspaces before missing untreated means become causal functionals. A deterministic smallest-two anchor convention maps every mask to the published rank-two count certificate of Pimentel--Alarcón, Boston, and Nowak, with Streinu--Theran pebble recognition and extraction as background. When the certificate passes, the observed local eigenspaces determine the global factor plane and an explicit complete-observed-law map recovers every untreated cohort-time mean. When it fails, the factor plane is generically nonunique, but the frozen primitive class does not imply causal-target nonidentification because an allowed tight-radius subclass has \(\mu=0\) throughout. The panel-specific corollary \(O_3\Rightarrow\) certificate acceptance remains strict for masks \(123,145,256,346\). Covariance PCA gives the unconditional squared-risk upper scale \(\min\{1,(Ns_N^2)^{-1}\}\), and robust profile-recentered moment inversion gives uniformly honest rectangles with upper half-width scale \(\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\). Construction of frontier-scale testing pairs on a nondegenerate frozen-model subclass and a model-specific honest-width lower bound remain open; \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\) is sufficient for consistency but is not necessary on the zero-target subclass.

project_justification.gap: Pimentel-Alarcón, Boston, and Nowak provide the rank-two deterministic count criterion, Streinu and Theran provide sparse-hypergraph pebble machinery, and Lei and Ross provide \(O_3\)-sufficient identification and regular APM inference. What remains distinct here is the positive causal transport from observed cohort moments through local eigenspaces and the relation kernel to an explicit complete-observed-law functional. Under the frozen primitive class, certificate failure proves factor-plane ambiguity but not different causal-target values, and no model-specific minimax or honest-width lower frontier is currently available.
project_justification.niche: The paper studies fixed-\(T\) causal recovery under deterministic cohort masks, separating generic factor-plane certification from causal-target identification. It combines the published certificate with an explicit observed-law mean functional, the strict panel-specific \(O_3\) containment witness, covariance-PCA upper risk, and finite-moment uniformly honest moment-inversion upper width near a singular relation margin.
project_justification.fill: The paper takes the published count and pebble results as inputs, proves that certificate acceptance yields complete-observed-law identification of every untreated cohort-time mean, and proves that certificate failure yields only generic factor-plane nonuniqueness without further primitive slack. It records strict \(O_3\) containment and develops unconditional covariance-PCA and robust-inversion upper guarantees. Frontier-scale testing-pair construction on a nondegenerate frozen-model subclass and the corresponding lower risk and width bounds are left open.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The joint cohort indicator, first-moment, and second-moment vector is estimated by coordinatewise median of means with a robust data-driven scale. Covariance PCA supplies the point estimator and its unconditional upper risk bound. Honest inference profiles distance to the compact primitive moment model and inverts a nonempty recentered \(\ell_\infty\) moment set, yielding uniform coverage and an upper width bound without a model-specific lower-width claim.

prose_updates.related_work: Pimentel-Alarcón, Boston, and Nowak provide the rank-two deterministic count criterion for generic subspace identification and matrix completion; that rank/count reduction is cited background rather than a novelty claim. Streinu and Theran supply sparse-hypergraph pebble recognition, extraction, component algorithms, and complexity. Király, Theran, and Tomioka identify generic completion through Jacobian closure and determinantal matroids. The distinct causal step here recovers cohort conditional eigenspaces from the complete observed law and proves that certificate acceptance yields an explicit functional for every missing untreated mean; certificate failure is interpreted only as generic factor-plane nonuniqueness. Lei and Ross provide the closest econometric setup: their \(O_3\) overlap-merging condition is sufficient for factor-plane identification and their APM estimator yields regular fixed-\(T\) inference. As a panel-specific corollary, \(O_3\) acceptance implies canonical certificate acceptance, while masks \(123,145,256,346\) are certificate-accepted and \(O_3\)-rejected. Srivastava and Pimentel-Alarcón establish reciprocal-singular-value projection perturbation, which supports the upper analysis but does not furnish a legal target-separating experiment in this frozen model. Yan and Wainwright study growing staggered-block matrices, Zhu studies weak-factor honesty costs, and Andrews and Cheng develop identification-robust inference; none supplies the still-open nondegenerate same-shell testing pair required for lower risk and width frontiers here. Liu, Wang, and Xu provide a concrete consumer through the \(\operatorname{fect}\) counterfactual-imputation workflow.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: Certificate failure makes the generic factor plane nonunique, but the frozen primitive class permits tight covariance and moment radii that force every cohort loading mean, and hence every causal target coordinate, to zero. Therefore certificate failure alone does not imply causal-target nonidentification, and \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\) is sufficient but not necessary for consistency on this class. Shell nonemptiness likewise supplies no target separation or primitive interior slack, so construction of a frontier-scale testing pair on a nondegenerate frozen-model subclass remains open, as does a model-specific lower bound for uniformly honest rectangle width. The covariance-PCA risk bound and robust profile-inversion honesty and width bounds are unconditional upper results. The profile inversion is an exact optimization over a compact primitive closure; numerical certification is outside the theorem.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The smallest-two anchor convention is deterministic, and the rank-two count criterion and pebble algorithms are published background. The paper claims the distinct positive causal transport: certificate acceptance makes every untreated cohort-time mean an explicit functional of the complete observed law. On certificate failure it claims generic nonuniqueness of the factor plane only, not observed-law-equivalent causal targets with different missing means. The panel-specific corollary \(O_3\Rightarrow\) certificate acceptance and its strict four-mask witness remain. Covariance PCA and the total profile-recentered robust moment inversion provide unconditional upper guarantees on nonempty singular-margin shells. The inversion uses an explicit \(\ell_\infty\) joint-moment norm, coordinatewise median-of-means estimation, a data-driven scale, finite-sample coverage, and an eventually empty full-box fallback. No minimax lower frontier, honest-width lower frontier, or necessity of \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\) is claimed under the frozen class; the required nondegenerate same-shell testing construction remains open.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem transports the published generic count certificate into an explicit complete-observed-law identifying functional when the certificate passes and proves factor-plane nonuniqueness as the exact unconditional algebraic consequence when it fails.
statement_notes.gap: Published count and pebble results do not derive the observed conditional eigenspaces or the causal mean map. Conversely, the frozen primitive model includes a nonempty tight-radius certificate-failing specification with a constant zero target, so complete-observed-law countermodels with different missing means cannot be asserted without further restrictions.
statement_notes.consumer: A passing certificate licenses complete untreated-mean recovery for Lei--Ross \(\operatorname{apm}\) and Liu--Wang--Xu \(\operatorname{fect}\); a failing certificate warns of factor-plane ambiguity but does not itself certify causal-target nonidentification.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\), and let
\[
\vartheta_0=\bigl(p,\Gamma,(m_c,H_c,\sigma_c)_{c=1}^C\bigr)
\]
be its primitive parameter.  Put \(q_0=4+\delta\).  Assumption \(\operatorname{ass:moment-radius}\), conditional Jensen's inequality, and the definition \(B=M_{\mathrm{mom}}^{1/q_0}\) give, for every \(c\),
\[
\|m_c\|_2
=\|\mathbb E_P(\lambda_i\mid C_i=c)\|_2
\le \{\mathbb E_P(\|\lambda_i\|_2^{q_0}\mid C_i=c)\}^{1/q_0}
\le B.
\tag{1}
\]
By \(\operatorname{ass:conditional-homoskedasticity}\),
\(\mathbb E_P(\|\varepsilon_i\|_2^2\mid C_i=c)=T\sigma_c^2\), because \(\operatorname{ass:error-mean}\) makes the conditional second moment equal to the trace of the conditional covariance.  Lyapunov's inequality and \(\operatorname{ass:moment-radius}\) therefore imply
\[
(T\sigma_c^2)^{q_0/2}
\le \mathbb E_P(\|\varepsilon_i\|_2^{q_0}\mid C_i=c)
\le M_{\mathrm{mom}},
\qquad
0\le\sigma_c\le B/\sqrt T\le B.
\tag{2}
\]
The actual conditional loading law witnesses \(m\in\mathfrak M_\lambda(H)\).  Equations (1)--(2), together with \(\operatorname{ass:positive-shares}\), \(\operatorname{ass:factor-normalization}\), \(\operatorname{ass:loading-covariance}\), \(\operatorname{ass:local-signal-gap}\), and \(\operatorname{ass:singular-shell}\), verify every constraint in \(\operatorname{def:primitive-moment-class}\).  Hence
\[
\vartheta_0\in\overline\Theta_N(s_N).
\tag{3}
\]

We next identify the observed moment vector generated by \(\vartheta_0\).  By \(\operatorname{ass:rank-two-factor-law}\) and \(\operatorname{ass:error-mean}\),
\[
\mathbb E_P\{J_cY_i(0)\mid C_i=c\}=\Gamma_{S_c}m_c.
\tag{4}
\]
Moreover, \(\operatorname{ass:loading-error-orthogonality}\) and \(\operatorname{ass:error-mean}\) make both conditional cross moments between \(\lambda_i\) and \(\varepsilon_i\) zero, while \(\operatorname{ass:conditional-homoskedasticity}\) gives the error second moment.  Thus
\[
\mathbb E_P\{J_cY_i(0)Y_i(0)'J_c'\mid C_i=c\}
=\Gamma_{S_c}(H_c+m_cm_c')\Gamma_{S_c}'+\sigma_c^2I_{|S_c|}.
\tag{5}
\]
Multiplication of (4)--(5) by \(p_c\), and inclusion of the cohort-indicator moment \(p_c\), agree coordinate by coordinate with the maps in \(\operatorname{def:moment-inversion}\) and \(\operatorname{def:robust-observed-moments}\).  Therefore
\[
g(\vartheta_0)=\theta(P).
\tag{6}
\]

Suppose first that \(N\ge2k_\alpha\).  Define
\[
E_N=\|\widehat\theta-\theta(P)\|_{\mathsf m},
\qquad
\mathcal E_N=\{E_N\le\widehat\rho_N\}.
\]
By (3), (6), and the definition of the profiled distance,
\[
d_N
=\min_{\vartheta\in\overline\Theta_N(s_N)}
\|g(\vartheta)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}
\le \|g(\vartheta_0)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}
=E_N.
\tag{7}
\]
On \(\mathcal E_N\), equations (6)--(7) yield
\[
\|g(\vartheta_0)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}
=E_N\le\widehat\rho_N\le d_N+\widehat\rho_N,
\]
so \(\vartheta_0\in\mathcal C_N\).  By the definition of the coordinatewise enclosing rectangle, \((\Gamma m_c)_{c=1}^C=\mu(P)\) then belongs to \(\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}}\).  The coverage part of \(\operatorname{lem:robust-moment-ball}\) gives
\[
\inf_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\Pr_P\{\mu(P)\in\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}}\}
\ge \inf_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}\Pr_P(\mathcal E_N)
\ge1-\alpha.
\tag{8}
\]
If \(N<2k_\alpha\), the rule instead returns \([-B,B]^{CT}\).  From \(\Gamma'\Gamma=I_2\) and (1),
\[
|\mu_{ct}(P)|\le\|\Gamma m_c\|_2\le\|m_c\|_2\le B,
\]
so the fallback rectangle covers with probability one.  This proves honesty for every \(N\).

For completeness, the returned endpoints are measurable.  Write \(K_N=\overline\Theta_N(s_N)\), let \((\vartheta_\ell)_{\ell\ge1}\) be a deterministic countable dense subset of this compact finite-dimensional set, and let \(h_j(\vartheta)\) be target coordinate \(j\).  The function
\[
d(x)=\min_{\vartheta\in K_N}\|g(\vartheta)-x\|_{\mathsf m}
\]
is continuous because
\[
|d(x)-d(y)|\le\|x-y\|_{\mathsf m}.
\]
For \(r>0\), define
\[
u_{j,k}(x,r)
=\sup\bigl\{h_j(\vartheta_\ell):
\|g(\vartheta_\ell)-x\|_{\mathsf m}<d(x)+r+k^{-1}\bigr\}.
\]
Each \(u_{j,k}\) is measurable as a countable supremum of measurable functions after assigning the fixed lower bound \(-B\) to an infeasible index.  Compactness, continuity of \(g\) and \(h_j\), and density imply
\[
\lim_{k\to\infty}u_{j,k}(x,r)
=\max_{\substack{\vartheta\in K_N:\\
\|g(\vartheta)-x\|_{\mathsf m}\le d(x)+r}}h_j(\vartheta).
\tag{9}
\]
Indeed, dense approximants prove the lower inequality in (9), while any sequence approaching the left-hand supremum has a convergent subsequence whose limit satisfies the weak constraint and proves the upper inequality.  Applying the same argument to \(-h_j\) gives a measurable lower endpoint.  Since \(\widehat\rho_N>0\) is measurable, (9) proves measurability of every endpoint evaluated at \((\widehat\theta,\widehat\rho_N)\).  The small-sample box is deterministic, so the entire rule is measurable.

It remains to bound width.  For arbitrary \(\vartheta,\widetilde\vartheta\in\mathcal C_N\), the triangle inequality and (7) give, without conditioning on \(\mathcal E_N\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\|g(\vartheta)-g(\widetilde\vartheta)\|_{\mathsf m}
&\le \|g(\vartheta)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}
 +\|g(\widetilde\vartheta)-\widehat\theta\|_{\mathsf m}\\
&\le2(d_N+\widehat\rho_N)\\
&\le2(E_N+\widehat\rho_N).
\end{aligned}
\tag{10}
\]
Both parameters in (10) belong to \(\overline\Theta_N(s_N)\).  Applying \(\operatorname{lem:observed-moment-inverse-modulus}\) and absorbing the factor two into its constant yields
\[
\max_{c\in[C]}
\|\Gamma m_c-\widetilde\Gamma\widetilde m_c\|_\infty
\le K\min\left\{1,\frac{E_N+\widehat\rho_N}{s_N}\right\}.
\tag{11}
\]
For each target coordinate, compactness makes both extrema in the enclosing rectangle attainable; choosing their two attaining parameters in (11) shows that the maximal rectangle half-width is at most one half of the right side of (11).  Since \(x\mapsto\min\{1,x\}\) is increasing and concave on \([0,\infty)\), Jensen's inequality and the expectation part of \(\operatorname{lem:robust-moment-ball}\) give
\[
\begin{aligned}
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\mathbb E_PW(\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}})
&\le K\min\left\{1,
\frac{\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\mathbb E_P(E_N+\widehat\rho_N)}{s_N}\right\}\\
&\le K\min\left\{1,\frac{K_\alpha}{\sqrt N s_N}\right\}\\
&\le C_\alpha\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{12}
\]
For \(N<2k_\alpha\), the normalized width is at most one.  Because \(s_N\le1\) and \(N<2k_\alpha\),
\[
\min\{1,(\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\}\ge(2k_\alpha)^{-1/2};
\]
increasing \(C_\alpha\) makes (12) valid also in this case.  Membership in \(\mathfrak I_{N,\alpha}\) follows from (8) and the small-sample argument, and the infimum bound follows by evaluating the infimum at \(\mathcal I_N^{\mathrm{inv}}\).  Finally, \(\mathsf F_N=\{N<2k_\alpha\}\) is deterministic and false whenever \(N\ge2k_\alpha\).  Its expected width contribution is then exactly zero, which divided by the positive scale \((\sqrt N s_N)^{-1}\) remains zero uniformly over \(s_N\in(0,1]\).  This proves every assertion.

For a sequence of nonempty shells with \(Ns_N^2\to\infty\), \(\operatorname{thm:minimax-frontier}\) gives
\[
0\le
\inf_{\widetilde\mu}\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\mathbb E_P L\{\widetilde\mu,\mu(P)\}
\le C_0\min\{1,(Ns_N^2)^{-1}\}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{13}
\]
This proves sufficiency.

To disprove necessity, use the allowed fixed primitive radii and legal equal-share family \((P_\eta)\) supplied by \(\operatorname{thm:four-mask-early-kill-negative}\).  That theorem supplies constants \(a,b,\eta_0>0\) such that, for \(0<|\eta|\le\eta_0\),
\[
a|\eta|\le s(P_\eta)\le b|\eta|,
\tag{14}
\]
and it states that \(\mu(P)=0\) for every law in the corresponding ambient model.  Choose \(\eta_N=\eta_0/(N+1)\) and define
\[
s_N=s(P_{\eta_N}).
\tag{15}
\]
The Gram representation in \(\operatorname{def:relation-operator}\) gives
\[
0\preceq A(P)=\sum_{c=1}^Cp_cJ_c'Q_cJ_c\preceq I_T,
\]
because \(0\preceq Q_c\preceq I_{|S_c|}\) and \(\sum_cp_c=1\).  Thus \(0<s_N\le1\).  Equation (15) also gives
\[
s_N\le s(P_{\eta_N})\le2s_N,
\]
so \(P_{\eta_N}\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)\) and every shell is nonempty.  By (14),
\[
Ns_N^2\le Nb^2\eta_0^2(N+1)^{-2}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{16}
\]
Every law in these shells belongs to the same tight-radius ambient model and therefore has \(\mu(P)=0\).  For the measurable estimator \(\widetilde\mu\equiv0\), the definition of \(L\) gives
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal P_N(s_N)}
\mathbb E_PL\{0,\mu(P)\}=0
\]
for every \(N\).  Together with (16), this is an explicit counterexample to necessity.
